response.answer:
A solar generator for home backup is a battery-powered system that can run household appliances during a power outage and recharge using solar panels, wall power, or sometimes a gas generator.

Unlike a traditional gas generator, it operates quietly, produces no exhaust, and can be used indoors.

For home backup, I recommend looking at systems from EcoFlow, Anker SOLIX, Bluetti, and Jackery.

Battery capacity (kWh) determines how long appliances can run. Inverter output (W) determines how many appliances you can power simultaneously.

Good for refrigerators, lighting, internet, and selected home circuits.

Shop

3,840 Wh battery, 6,000 W output, 120/240V support. Up to 3,200 W solar input.

Good for higher-power appliances and expandable backup systems.

Shop

Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus

5,040 Wh battery, 7,200 W output, 120/240V support.

Good for larger loads and whole-home backup configurations with additional batteries.

These specifications are based on published manufacturer information and recent comparisons. 
TheOutagePlan
+2

For a typical refrigerator, router, lights, and a few small electronics drawing an average of 250 W, a 4 kWh battery might provide roughly 13–14 hours of backup after allowing for conversion losses. Solar charging can extend that duration, depending on sunlight and panel size.

A home electrical-panel connection requires a compatible transfer switch or backup panel installed correctly; never backfeed a household outlet.
